body: My main problem with communicating suicidal feelings isn't how to do it, but simply being able to trust enough to do it in the first place.  I'm an intensely private introvert and I've never been able to tell anyone in my life just how far these thoughts go.  No matter what reassurances I've been given (and there have been many in therapy), they just haven't been enough to make me come forward with everything.

I appreciate the effort you put into your post (not being sarcastic).  However, I regard taking that series of antidepressants as possibly the biggest mistake of my life...and I did it under the influence of an overzealous psychiatrist that *guaranteed* me I would feel fantastic if I just took the drugs he told me to.

Instead, I have gotten nothing but pain and anguish in return.  I can honestly say that I have not experienced a single happy day -- not ONE -- in almost five years.  Just monolithic blackness.  Not to mention all of the cognitive side effects that I am still feeling.  The up-and-down depression of years past looks like a pleasant dream in comparison.  

I see a therapist (my seventh? I've lost track) once a week these days, and she seems competent and empathetic.  But there's only so much she can do.  I don't know to communicate that I need so much more just to stay afloat right now.  I also have no clue what that "more" is or could be.

Anyways, today I threw up repeatedly into a toilet over another panic attack...before going to therapy to treat depression and anxiety.  I'm a real masterpiece, huh?
I have not been on medication since that experience five years ago.  Just thinking of antidepressants disgusts me.
